opex.name: Operating, selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Running the stores, clubs, warehouses and head office.

follow100Note: The stores earned $4.18 of operating profit from every $100 of revenue; an $813M investment gain, tax and partners' shares left $3.17. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.
footerNote: Net profit shown is the $5,494M attributable to Walmart; consolidated net income was $5,678M, of which $184M belongs to noncontrolling interests. Per-share figures are shown split-adjusted for the 3-for-1 stock split distributed February 23, 2024; as originally reported before the split, GAAP EPS was $2.03 and adjusted EPS was $1.80.
oneTimers: Other (gains) and losses was an $813M gain this quarter versus a $3,848M gain a year ago — unrealized fair-value moves on equity investments Walmart holds, led by Symbotic and Asda debt securities and partly offset by JD.com. Adjusted EPS of $0.60 (split-adjusted; $1.80 as reported before the 3-for-1 split) excludes the net-of-tax effect of the investment gain ($0.08 per share split-adjusted; $0.23 pre-split).

The year-ago quarter included $849M of business reorganization and restructuring charges in Walmart International, which flatters the reported 30.4% operating-income growth; adjusted operating income, which excludes those year-ago charges, rose 13.2%.
otherDetail: Interest of $549M, net, offset by an $813M gain on equity and other investments — mostly fair-value moves, led by a higher Symbotic share price and Asda debt securities, partly offset by a lower JD.com share price.

segments.name: Walmart U.S.
segments.note: Stores and eCommerce in the United States — comparable sales rose 4.0%, eCommerce rose 17%, and segment operating income rose 12.9% to $6,075M as the gross margin rate widened 64 basis points.

segments.name: Walmart International
segments.note: Stores and eCommerce outside the U.S. — net sales rose 13.0% in constant currency, led by Flipkart, Walmex and China; eCommerce rose 44% and segment operating income was $1,438M versus $289M a year ago.

segments.name: Sam's Club U.S.
segments.note: Walmart's warehouse clubs in the United States — comparable sales rose 3.1% excluding fuel, eCommerce rose 17%, and membership income rose 10.0%.

segments.name: Membership & other income
segments.note: Membership fees from Sam's Club and Walmart+, plus other income — small, but nearly cost-free.

sources.label: Form 10-K, fiscal year ended January 31, 2024 (SEC EDGAR)

takeaways.text: Operating income rose 30.4% to $7,254M on 5.7% revenue growth — the gross margin rate widened 39 basis points, led by Walmart U.S., membership income grew 13.0%, and global eCommerce sales rose 23%, passing $100B for the full year. On an adjusted basis, which adds back $849M of reorganization charges in the year-ago quarter, operating income still grew 13.2%.
takeaways.title: Operating income grew far faster than sales

takeaways.text: Below the operating line, Walmart booked an $813M gain on equity and other investments — mostly fair-value moves on stakes it holds. A year ago the same line was a $3,848M gain; that swing is the main reason headline profit fell 12.4% to $5,494M even though the stores had a much stronger quarter. Adjusted EPS of $0.60, split-adjusted, strips the gain out, versus GAAP EPS of $0.68.
takeaways.title: A smaller paper gain, not weaker stores

takeaways.text: Walmart raised its annual dividend 9% to $0.83 per share on a post-split basis — its largest increase in over a decade and its 51st consecutive annual rise — after generating $35.7B in operating cash flow and $15.1B in free cash flow for the full year.
takeaways.title: Dividend raised 9%

verdict: Walmart's revenue rose 5.7% to $173.4B and operating income jumped 30.4% as U.S. comparable sales rose 4.0% and eCommerce grew 23% — but headline profit fell 12.4% to $5.5B because a year ago an even bigger $3.8B paper gain on its investment stakes had flattered the comparison.
